newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian short OLOs to feel further heat.
newsitem.headline: Belgian short OLOs to feel further heat.

text.p: Belgian short-term OLO yields, driven up in recent weeks by domestic selling, are likely to remain under pressure, traders said on Wednesday.

"The (yield) curve has seriously flattened in recent weeks and it looks like this will continue," one Luxembourg-based trader said. But inflation news would determine whether the short-end's resistance would cave in or not.
"As long as inflation is not clearly visible, the (upward yield) movement will still be restricted, but one data release could get the train going," he said.
One trader said a number of Belgian banks had liquidated short paper in recent weeks as they believed a period of low yields was grinding to a halt.
"We still regularly see large selling orders for one-, two-, three-year paper," he said.
Traders said the dollar remained the main worry, noting the mark had come under renewed pressure from the dollar and was inches away from 1.90 -- the level expected to trigger Bundesbank action.
One believed Buba action was even possible on Thursday.
Traditionally, the Belgian and French francs firmed when the mark weakened against the dollar. "Not any more, however," he said.
Another trader voiced concern about the impact of rising short-term rates on the European single currency project.
"Southern European currencies will definitely suffer, but so will Germany and France, since interest charges will be higher than they bargained for," he said.
